name: search_code
description: Literal, case-insensitive text search over the source files of the private codebase (config/ is never searched). Returns JSON: query (echoed back), query_valid, count (how many lines matched), shown, truncated (true when count is larger than shown), index_age (how old the prebuilt index is, or a note that it was not used when source is disk), and results, a list of {path, line, excerpt} in path order. A search that matches nothing is a success: count 0, results [], query_valid true. It means the text is not in the searched files, so try a shorter or different term rather than the same query again; if source is index, also check index_age, because an old index can miss recent changes. A malformed search is an error, never an empty result: an empty or whitespace-only query, a query over 200 characters, or a path_glob that is not a valid glob. Responses are capped: concise shows at most 5 results with excerpts cut to 80 characters, detailed at most 20 with excerpts cut to 160; truncated says when more lines matched than are shown.

query.description: Text to find, matched literally and case-insensitively against each line. It is not a regex and not a query language. 1 to 200 characters; an empty or longer query is an error.

path_glob.description: Only search files whose path matches this glob, relative to the repository root, such as src/**/*.ts or src/export/*.{ts,tsx}; the wildcards are * ? [ ] { }. Pass null to search every file. Use it when a plain search matches many unrelated files. It narrows what is searched and costs nothing extra. A glob that is not valid is an error. A glob only includes files; it cannot exclude with ! or |, so to skip a directory, name the directories you want instead, such as src/{api,components}/**.

response_format.description: concise: at most 5 results with short excerpts; the cheap choice, use it first. detailed: at most 20 results with longer excerpts; use it only when a concise search was truncated and you need more.

source.description: index: read the prebuilt index; fast, and index_age says how old it is. Use this first. disk: read the files themselves; slower, always current. Use it only when index_age is more than a day old, or when a search you expect to match returns count 0.

examples.note: typical: a first search over the whole codebase, cheap format, prebuilt index
hard: restrict to source files with a glob, read the current files, and ask for more results after a concise search was truncated
